key_insight: UniHam benchmarks Hamiltonian learning with full spin–orbit coupling (SOC), revealing why reconstruction accuracy alone cannot establish reliability for electronic-property prediction.
engineering_relevance: Reliable learned Hamiltonians could reduce reliance on costly DFT calculations while supporting electronic-property inference across diverse materials.
method: Construct 100,000+ DFT-computed complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians with full SOC across 72 elements.
Benchmark two representative state-of-the-art models under a standardized protocol.
Evaluate reconstruction, composition/symmetry out-of-distribution generalization, and downstream property prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluations reveal SOC- and element-dependent failure modes, substantial differences in compositional OOD robustness, and the need for spectral-level assessment.
watch_item: Broad dataset coverage does not guarantee transfer to unseen materials; validate spectral and downstream-property accuracy under relevant distribution shifts.
paper_title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
